title: Intent-aware prefetch amortization benchmark — sketch
body:
Summary:

This is a working sketch of microbenchmarks comparing three prefetch strategies for KV/prefix prepopulation: (1) no-prefetch (on-demand only), (2) naive-prefetch (static X-token lookahead on session start), and (3) intent-aware-prefetch (predictive prefetch using a lightweight classifier + recent-session pattern matching). Goal: quantify latency improvements, hit-rate gains, and net cost change after amortization across session lengths and traffic mixes.

Key takeaways (early):
- Intent-aware prefetch reduces p99 tail by up to ~28% for conversational sessions with high repetition (short-turn followups), vs no-prefetch.
- Compared to naive-prefetch, intent-aware reduces unnecessary compute preload by ~35% (less wasted amortization), yielding lower net cost for low-turn sessions while preserving most latency benefits for long sessions.
- Break-even point (where naive-prefetch amortization pays off vs no-prefetch) varies by hardware and session length; we observed it around 6–9 turns on A100-80GB under our trace.

Motivation and framing:
- Prefetching KV/prefix state can hide some of the decoder latency by overlapping compute for likely next tokens/segments. However, prefetch cost is incurred even when the session diverges — hence the amortization question. An "intent-aware" approach tries to only prefetch when the predicted probability of using the prefetched state exceeds a threshold.

Experiment setup (short):
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB per worker; baseline runs repeated on H100-80GB for cross-check (smaller run).
- Model: open-architecture LLM (Llama-2 13B-like quantized run) with KV cache support.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime build v0.72-experiments (PR 1427), batching knobs: dynamic batching, session affinity enabled.
- Workloads: three synthetic traces derived from production-sampled anonymized sessions (see linked artifact INFR-2389):
  * short-chat (70%): median turns/session=3, high single-turn followups
  * mixed-app (25%): median turns/session=9, bursts of long sessions and short ones
  * long-convo (5%): median turns/session=28, higher token lengths per turn
- Traffic envelope: 200 qps steady-state with Poisson spike experiments to 800 qps for microburst checks.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 per-request latency (end-to-end), amortized per-session latency (sum of user-visible latency + prefetch overheads divided by turns), token-cost ($/1M tokens derived from infra hourly + GPU utilization), prefetch hitrate, wasted-prefetch ratio (prefetches not used).

Approaches implemented:
- no-prefetch: no speculative work, on-demand KV population only when request reaches server.
- naive-prefetch(X): on session start, server kicks off prefetch for next X tokens/segments (X=64 in this run). No classifier.
- intent-aware-prefetch (conservative/aggressive): small classifier (100k-parameter logistic over turn features) predicts probability p_use; prefetch executed if p_use > theta. Conservative theta=0.6, Aggressive theta=0.3. Classifier trained on prior-month session patterns; inference cost folded into lightweight CPU overhead measured separately.

Representative results (mixed-app trace, A100 runs):

1) Latency percentiles (ms) — per-request e2e (including network and decode):

| Strategy                  | p50  | p90  | p99  |
|---------------------------|------|------|------|
| no-prefetch               | 78   | 210  | 820  |
| naive-prefetch (X=64)     | 70   | 180  | 610  |
| intent-aware (conservative)| 72   | 185  | 590  |
| intent-aware (aggressive) | 69   | 170  | 560  |

Notes: p99 improvement vs no-prefetch: naive 25.6%, intent-aware(aggr) 31.7%. p50 relatively similar because prefetch mainly affects tail.

2) Prefetch hitrate and wasted-prefetch ratio (sessionized):

| Strategy                  | hitrate (%) | wasted-prefetch (%) |
|---------------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| naive-prefetch (X=64)     | 71          | 29                   |
| intent-aware (conservative)| 82          | 18                   |
| intent-aware (aggressive) | 76          | 24                   |

Interpretation: conservative threshold pushes up precision (fewer wasted prefetches) at the expense of slightly lower hitrate vs aggressive; naive spends most but still gets hits because X covers many common continuations.

3) Amortized latency per session (ms per turn) — includes prefetch CPU/GPU overheads apportioned to session when prefetch executed: 

| Strategy                  | short-chat (median 3 turns) | mixed-app (median 9 turns) | long-convo (median 28 turns) |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------|
| no-prefetch               | 210                         | 190                         | 170                           |
| naive-prefetch (X=64)     | 240                         | 170                         | 150                           |
| intent-aware (conservative)| 220                        | 175                         | 152                           |
| intent-aware (aggressive) | 235                         | 168                         | 148                           |

Breakdown: naive-prefetch penalizes short sessions due to wasted prefetch overhead; intent-aware reduces that penalty and preserves amortization for long sessions.

4) Cost sensitivity (approx $ per 10k requests, normalized to no-prefetch=1.0):

| Strategy                  | cost ratio (10k reqs) |
|---------------------------|------------------------|
| no-prefetch               | 1.00                   |
| naive-prefetch (X=64)     | 1.18                   |
| intent-aware (conservative)| 1.08                  |
| intent-aware (aggressive) | 1.12                   |

Notes: cost model includes GPU-hours with utilization delta, small CPU classifier cost, and additional transient memory for prefetched state. Naive shows highest cost due to wasted GPU cycles that cannot always be overlapped.

Microburst behavior (spike to 800 qps):
- No-prefetch exhibits steep p99 spikes and queueing; naive-prefetch increases contention because of background prefetch jobs triggering during bursts — exacerbates p99 when capacity constrained.
- Intent-aware (conservative) showed the best burst resilience: lower background activity and higher selective prefetch prevented adding load during critical spike windows.

Operational considerations and caveats:
- Classifier drift: the predictive model needs periodic retraining as session intents shift (weekly cadence suggested). Monitoring should include precision/recall of prefetch decisions and drift alerts (Confluence doc linked).
- Prefetch scheduling: prefer background slotting with preemptible lower-priority worker threads so forecasts don't steal critical decode slots in constrained times. We experimented with two modes: background-queued (safer) and immediate-worker (faster but riskier). Background-queued + conservative threshold was the safest for SLAs.
- Cost accounting: must ensure amortized accounting rolls prefetch GPU time into customer/session cost buckets (otherwise product bill confusion).
- Cold-start sessions: warmup/priming heuristics still valuable; combine intent-aware prefetch with lightweight prefix caching to speed first turn for known application patterns (e.g., chatbots).

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Run the same matrix on H100 and multi-tenant virtualized GPU scenarios to check sensitivity shown in multi-tenant/slot-contention docs.
- Sweep thresholds (theta) continuously and track the frontier of hitrate vs wasted-prefetch to derive recommended default.
- Evaluate classifier versions that include prompt embeddings (cheap distil) vs token-features only; measure classifier ingestion latency cost tradeoffs.
- Create a small in-console visualization (per-route) that shows prefetch effectiveness over last 7 days (p50/p90/p99 + wasted-prefetch rate).

Appendix: quick ascii trend (amortized latency vs median turns) — rough sketch:

Turns per session ---> 1    3    6    9    15    28
no-prefetch           | 220  210  200  190  178   170
naive-prefetch (X=64) | 260  240  200  170  158   150
intent-aware (cons)    | 230  220  195  175  160   152
intent-aware (aggr)    | 255  235  195  168  155   148

(Visualization note: lines converge for long sessions where amortization dominates; divergence at short session lengths.)

Questions for review:
- Acceptable default theta for intent-aware? (we recommend conservative 0.6 as default with per-customer override).
- Operational policy during bursts: should prefetch be globally disabled when cluster load > 80%? (current experiments suggest yes for naive, optional for intent-aware).
- Billing model: do we expose prefetch inefficiency as a separate metric or hide it within per-token costs?

Tags/labels for follow-ups: prefetched-state-accounting, classifier-drift, prefetch-scheduling, burst-policy, PR-1427-runbook.
